summary: The published AI+Cybersecurity prompt concerns scams, impersonation and fraud. The old ActionProof refund-policy idea does not directly address it. A job-offer verification workflow may fit, but novelty and AI benefit must be disproved or measured before committing. This is research, not a build or prize prediction.

sources.title: ForgeHacks released track prompts
sources.supports: Cybersecurity asks for an AI-powered solution that helps people recognize, prevent, verify, or respond to scams, impersonation and fraud; Education and other tracks also published.

ideas.title: OfferProof: verify a suspicious job offer
ideas.problem: Students receiving plausible recruiter messages need a safe next action before sharing data or paying.
ideas.differentiation: Generate a claim-by-claim verification checklist and an independent contact path; the system must explicitly say when legitimacy is unverified. Compare decisions to a fixed warning-list baseline.
ideas.scope: Text-only, three synthetic employer/job scenarios, guided verification and evidence log; no automated declaration that a real company is safe.
ideas.weakest_assumption: A judge may see only an LLM wrapper around FTC advice. Test whether the interaction produces fewer unsafe actions than a static warning list on blinded cases.

ideas.title: ScamRehearsal: interactive fake recruiter
ideas.problem: Students may know warning signs yet fail under pressure.
ideas.differentiation: Adaptive decisions with a deterministic answer key and replay; however very close to multiple existing projects.
ideas.scope: Two safe fictional scenarios, no actual victim outreach.
ideas.weakest_assumption: Clear overlap with prior Devpost entries; would need unusually strong measured learning transfer to justify.

ideas.title: Tutor Autopsy: diagnose persuasive wrong answers
ideas.problem: Learners memorize answers without understanding why a plausible explanation fails.
ideas.differentiation: Executable counterexamples and concept links, with AI explanation evaluated against a deterministic test oracle; fits Education prompt rather than Cybersecurity.
ideas.scope: Three bounded misconceptions and one working learning loop.
ideas.weakest_assumption: Need evidence of better concept transfer, and prior similar education projects should be checked before ranking it higher.

rejected_previous_candidate: ActionProof is technically interesting but fails direct alignment with the released AI+Cybersecurity prompt; do not build it for that track.
critic_questions: Does OfferProof add measurable value over FTC text and ordinary search?
Can a user genuinely verify independently without trusting a contact URL supplied by the suspect message or a hallucinated LLM?
Does a text-only demo make AI essential, or would deterministic extraction and a form be enough?
Which track has the strongest complete demo under one-person, zero-dollar constraints?
What observed prior winners, if any, are relevant? This draft has no ForgeHacks past winners because the event is a first edition.
unknowns: No user interviews or independent usability evidence yet.
Current competing ForgeHacks entries are unknown.
No live AI model, cost, or evaluation results have been produced.
The final product direction should not pass go until the critic's objections and a baseline test are addressed.
